editorial_reason: ProofWiki explicitly defines a measurable space as a set equipped with a sigma-algebra. It does not require a measure, probability distribution or topological structure. The independently screened sigma-algebra meaning supplies an exact noncircular prerequisite; measure space is a further context with an additional measure map.

ProofWiki defines a probability space as a measure space with total measure one. Probability measure countable additivity and nonnegativity are part of the measure definition; normalized total mass is a distinctive condition. This can be a target for stochastic-process and conditional-expectation meanings after independently screening the measurable-space and measure prerequisites. The empty space admits no probability measure with P(Ω)=1, so it is excluded by the axioms, not by an arbitrary extra clause.

The direct ProofWiki random-variable page separates the general measurable-space-valued and real-valued formulations. Real-valued measurability has an equivalent half-infinite-interval inverse-image criterion. These two variants have different codomain scopes; do not merge their object contexts silently or confuse a 'continuous random variable' with a continuous sample path. General random variable and real-valued random variable can be displayed in appropriate educational ordering and linked to probability/measurable spaces when independently screened.
